name: FragmentViewer
intent: Renders a That Open Fragments (.frag) model with orbit, zoom and click-to-select — the same runtime the WC3 engineering viewers use. Fills its parent, reports the picked element, and releases its WebGL context on unmount.
when: Showing a single BIM/engineering model inside a product surface
Filling the canvas of a map/site workspace with a building rather than a basemap
A picked element must drive surrounding panels (selection is reported, not owned)
whenNot: Geospatial basemaps, geofences or asset pins -> use Map (mapbox-gl)
Whole-project federations of gigabyte scale -> stream through APS; Fragments loads one model into browser memory
IFC files -> convert to .frag first (IfcImporter); this widget deliberately avoids the 23 MB web-ifc wasm

chooseOver.component: Embedding a third-party BIM viewer in an iframe
chooseOver.because: FragmentViewer renders in-page, themes with the surrounding surface and reports selection back to React.

allowedPlacement: a parent with a bounded height (the canvas fills its container)
forbiddenPlacement: inside a scrolling container with auto height (the canvas collapses to zero)
more than a couple per page (each instance holds a WebGL context)
commonMistakes: Omitting workerUrl or passing a bare specifier — a bundled library cannot resolve @thatopen/fragments/worker to a runtime URL, so the model silently never loads
Mounting it in an auto-height parent, which gives the canvas zero height
Passing a new inline onSelectionChange identity expecting a reload — handlers are held in refs precisely so the WebGL context survives re-renders

extracted: canvas-owned scene / camera / OrbitControls / render loop
debounced fragments.update on camera move, forced on rest
click raycast to highlight + selection callback

notes: three and @thatopen/fragments are OPTIONAL peerDependencies — only apps importing this widget install them (~900 KB)
pin @thatopen/fragments to the version that authored the .frag files; the WC3 dataset catalog records 3.4.6
scope is one model: multi-model federation, geospatial placement, isolation and QTO are deliberately out

usage: Use FragmentViewer to enhance your user interface. This component provides a consistent, accessible, and well-designed solution for this use case.
FragmentViewer integrates seamlessly with other components in the design system. Follow the established patterns and guidelines to ensure consistency across your application.

props.name: src
props.description: URL of the `.frag` model to display.

props.name: fallbackSrc
props.description: Optional model URL used when `src` cannot be loaded.

props.name: modelId
props.description: Stable id for the model within the viewport. Defaults to `src`.

props.name: workerUrl
props.description: URL of the Fragments web worker — required, because a bundled library cannot resolve the `@thatopen/fragments/worker` specifier to a runtime URL. In a Vite app: `import workerUrl from "@thatopen/fragments/worker?url"`.

props.name: background
props.description: Scene background. `null` leaves the canvas transparent.

props.name: showLogo
props.description: Show the underlying SDK logo over the canvas. Defaults to false.

props.name: fitAnimation
props.description: Animate the camera when first framing the model on load. Default true. Set false to jump to the framed position instantly (e.g. when an outer transition already zooms the viewer in).

props.name: fitCategories
props.description: Frame only the elements whose IFC category matches one of these patterns (e.g. the building shell) instead of the whole model. Pass a stable (module-level) array — a new array each render reloads the model.

props.name: fitFactor
props.description: Multiply the fit distance. Default 1; below 1 frames tighter (closer).

props.name: markers
props.description: Point markers drawn in the model — workers, sensors, anything with a position.

props.name: markerRadius
props.description: Marker radius in model units. Defaults to ~1/300th of the model diagonal.

props.name: markersOccluded
props.description: Let geometry hide markers behind it. Default false — markers read through the model, like pins.

props.name: selectFloorsOnly
props.description: Floor-only picking: a click selects (isolates) the storey the element belongs to instead of the element itself, so individual elements aren't selectable. Requires the IFC to have storeys.

props.name: ...props
props.description: All standard HTML attributes are supported.

anatomy.description: FragmentViewer is composed of the following parts:

bestPractices.title: Use semantic props
bestPractices.description: Use the component's built-in props rather than className overrides.

bestPractices.title: Don't override core styles
bestPractices.description: Avoid using className to override the component's fundamental styling.

bestPractices.title: Provide accessible labels
bestPractices.description: Include proper ARIA labels for screen reader users.

bestPractices.title: Don't skip accessibility
bestPractices.description: Never omit accessibility attributes for interactive components.

bestPractices.title: Handle all states
bestPractices.description: Account for loading, error, empty, and success states.

bestPractices.title: Don't ignore edge cases
bestPractices.description: Avoid showing broken UI when data is missing or loading.
